payload.acceptance_criteria: a repository upgraded with basicly install carries a post-merge hook that folds pending shards, asserted on a repository that already had a ledger before the install rather than only on a fresh one; the kits reference stops claiming install leaves nothing to run until it is true
payload.description:
When a repository upgrades with basicly install, I want its post-merge hook folding pending shards, so I can stop the trunk log ceasing to be the readable history on a repository worked from two machines.

Found by the terminal canary after a live v0.14.1 install and filed there as term-ftosv. The kit file is vendored and unwired: .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py sets HOOK_NAME to post-merge, and grepping cli.py at e2451c95 for install_hook or post-merge finds only the tier kit's installer and the pre-commit stage activation. The install line says it activated pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push, and ls of .git/hooks confirms no post-merge against a control of three hooks present.

The contrast control is what makes this a wiring gap rather than a design choice: cli.TIER_HOOK_INSTALLER and cmd_tier_hook run the tier kit's identically shaped install_hook.py as a subprocess and it is a named install step. The engine has the mechanism and uses it for one kit and not the other. Same divergence as basicly-cb61y44, where the standalone installer wrote a rule the engine path did not.

The canary also named the trap: _setup_tracker returns early on an existing ledger, so a fix placed there skips every consumer that already has one - exactly the repositories that have shards to fold.

Not data loss. The fold reads both globs so reads stay correct; the cost is that shards are never consolidated and the trunk stops being the history a person reads.

docs/reference/kits.md states that basicly install brings all three kits with nothing else to run, which is false while this step is missing.
payload.requirements: the engine runs the kit's own installer as a subprocess exactly as it does for the tier kit, holding no kit import, and passes the ledger the same way the standalone package does. The step is not placed inside _setup_tracker, whose early return would skip every existing consumer.
payload.title: wire the tracker shard hook the way the tier hook is already wired

payload.acceptance_criteria: the markdown basicly generates passes markdownlint with default rules, measured the way the canary measures it - projections copied into a directory with a consumer config and no basicly config present - with a ragged table as the positive control proving the rule is active
payload.description:
When a consumer lints their repository with default markdownlint rules, I want the markdown basicly generated into it to pass, so I can stop shipping output that fails a gate we also ship.

Found by the terminal canary after a v0.14.1 install, filed there as term-fawxo, and blocking their commit. Reproduced here, which is the part that matters: copying this repository's own .claude and .agents projections plus AGENTS.md into a directory carrying a consumer-shaped markdownlint config produces 20 MD060 table-column-style errors. The canary sees 62 because their projection set is larger.

This repository passes only because .markdownlint-cli2.yaml disables MD060 for itself, with a recorded reason under basicly-jaz4: the rule fires when one cell of an aligned table is edited without re-padding, and --fix will not re-pad. That reason is about hand-edited markdown. It was never shipped, so a consumer whose config says default true gets the rule and our output fails it.

The standard this misses is our own. The same config file says a violation in a projected file means a template or catalog source regressed, fix it there and rebuild. The generator is emitting markdown that is not lint-clean and the rule was turned off rather than the output fixed.

The canary also reports 24 MD022 and MD032 errors inside the Commit delta auto-generated section that basicly release writes. That half does NOT reproduce here: this repository's own CHANGELOG.md passes the same consumer config with exit 0, so their 24 need their file to diagnose and are not confirmed as ours.

The first probe I ran reported zero and was wrong: markdownlint merges the repository's own config even under --config, so the rule was disabled in my own measurement. A deliberately ragged table as a positive control did not fire either, which is what exposed it. The numbers above are from a directory that carries no basicly config.
payload.requirements: the fix is at the source or the projector rather than by disabling a rule in the consumer's config, because the consumer's lint config is theirs and a rule we silence for ourselves is not a rule we may silence for them. Whatever is chosen, the scoping advice the install prints must name the same paths as the fix.
payload.title: our generated markdown fails a rule we disabled only for ourselves

payload.text:
The CHANGELOG half is settled and is not ours. Grepping the whole tree for 'Commit delta' returns CHANGELOG.md and the ledger only - no source file, no script, no workflow - against a positive control that the string does exist in CHANGELOG.md. Stronger, because absent today is not absent ever: git log --all -S over src, .scripts and any .py returns nothing, against a control of 4 commits when the same search is scoped to CHANGELOG.md. This repository's one such section was written by a human commit, b0bf6daf, and carries the blank line. So basicly release has never emitted that heading and the canary's 12 sections came from something else; a hand fix there stays fixed. Bound: only this repository was searched.

The canary's escaped-pipe finding is a requirement on any projector fix, recorded before the work starts. Their first re-padding attempt refused to write because a cell containing an escaped pipe, in a table documenting the pipe operator, split into a phantom extra column and would have added an empty cell to every row. Split on unescaped pipes only, (?<!\\)\|. A naive split silently widens the table and the damage reads as padding, which is the shape that passes review.

Their verification standard is the one to hold a fix to: refuse to write unless the parsed cell text is identical, then confirm at the diff level that the removed and added lines are byte-identical after squashing spaces, dashes and colons. Two paths sharing no step.

Withdrawn rather than shipped, and the reason is a measurement rather than a preference. The wiring worked - cmd_tracker_hook mirrored the tier one and installed correctly on a repository that already had a ledger, so the canary's early-return trap was avoided. But on the merge that followed, the hook folded the shard and could not commit it: its message carries no record id and tracker-commit-msg, written by the same install, refuses that. So in any basicly repository the hook folds, stages and leaves a dirty tree after every merge, which is the objection that made the clean-tree guard exist in the first place.

The two remaining shapes were not real. Staging without committing is the dirty tree by design. Shipping it as it stands is shipping a hook that cannot commit.

So the engine does not get the hook. It already folds at commit_tracker_state with an id the gate accepts, and docs/reference/kits.md said the opposite - that install brings all three with nothing else to run - which is corrected here. The post-merge hook remains the standalone answer, where there is no commit-msg gate and its commit succeeds.

What is left undone and is the real fix: a repository worked from two machines accumulates a shard from the other machine until the next tracker write or landing folds it. Self-healing in an active repository, not in a quiet one. An engine-side fold on merge, committing the way the engine already does, is filed as the follow-on.

payload.acceptance_criteria: a plain git merge or pull in a repository with basicly folds any shard it brought in and commits it with a record id the commit-msg gate accepts, leaving the tree clean; a tree carrying work in progress is left untouched, asserted against a control showing the shard surviving
payload.description:
When a repository with basicly is worked from two machines on one branch, I want a shard arriving from the other machine folded at the merge, so I can keep the trunk log readable without waiting for the next landing.

The kit's post-merge hook cannot do this for a basicly repository: its commit carries no record id and tracker-commit-msg, written by the same install, refuses it, so it folds and leaves a dirty tree. That is why basicly-jmp6561 was withdrawn rather than shipped.

The engine already has what the hook lacks. commit_tracker_state folds and commits with an id the gate accepts, and merge_worktree calls it at the landing. What is missing is the same fold reached from a plain git merge or pull rather than only from a loop landing.

The gap is bounded and self-healing in an active repository: the next tracker write or landing folds whatever arrived. It is a quiet repository that accumulates, which is the canary's case between landings.
payload.requirements: no bypass of any gate: the commit carries a real record id rather than skipping the hook that asks for one. The engine reaches the fold through the seam it already uses rather than a second mechanism, and a repository without basicly keeps the kit's post-merge hook as its answer.
payload.title: fold a shard at the merge from the engine side

payload.acceptance_criteria: the catalog sources behind the projections carry consistent tables, the projections pass markdownlint under a consumer config with no basicly config present, catalog-lint refuses a table whose delimiter row does not match its cells, and the canary's remaining count goes to zero in one step rather than partly
payload.description:
When a catalog source carries a table whose delimiter row is unpadded while its cells are padded, I want the authoring gate to refuse it, so I can stop shipping markdown that fails a consumer's default lint.

Found by the terminal canary as term-fawxo, blocking their upgrade commit on 62 errors after they cleared their own 31. Reproduced here: this repository's projections produce 20 MD060 errors under a consumer config with no basicly config present, against a ragged table as the positive control.

All 20 are style compact and the cause is one shape. A table writes a padded header and padded cells while leaving the delimiter row bare - pipe dash dash dash pipe - so markdownlint infers compact from the delimiter and then objects to every padded cell. The table is internally inconsistent, which is what the rule exists to catch.

basicly-jaz4 disabled MD060 here for a reason that does not govern this: it named an ALIGNED table, where editing one cell forces a hand re-pad of every other pipe and fix will not do it. None of these are aligned. The remedy is to pad the delimiter row, two characters per column, once.
payload.requirements: the fix is in the catalog sources rather than the projector, so the projector never rewrites authored prose. Any later normaliser splits on unescaped pipes only, because an escaped pipe in a table documenting the pipe operator splits into a phantom column and the damage reads as padding. basicly-jaz4 is annotated rather than left reading as blanket cover.
payload.title: pad the delimiter rows and gate the rule that caught them
